claim: Advisory energy ordering alone is not a verifier-facing optimality certificate. A low-energy first candidate can fail true weak optimality for both minimization and maximization unless deterministic verifier or certificate premises are supplied.

commands.command: cd lean-mathlib && lake env lean Proofs/ZenoEnergyAdvisoryBoundary.lean

negative_knowledge: A learned energy ranker can prioritize search but cannot prove verifier optimality from ordering alone.
Low energy for an invalid or suboptimal candidate is harmless only because deterministic verification and fallback/certificate checks remain authoritative.
limits: The theorem is an abstract counterexample over finite candidates, not a quantitative model-performance claim.
It strengthens the advisory boundary but does not prove UPBA v2 bounded-grid completeness.
Production-adjacent use still requires real replay, source custody, coverage profiles, and deterministic fallback or suffix-bound certificates.
